name: Austin
metaDescription: Industry-specific market reports for Austin, Texas. Landscaping, roofing, HVAC, and pest control intelligence with local demand, pricing, and competitive data.
ogDescription: Local market reports for Austin operators — demand, competition, pricing, and growth opportunities by industry.
intro: Austin's growth has reshaped every home-service market in the metro. Residential build-out across Williamson, Hays, and east Travis means demand is moving faster than competitor capacity can keep up.
statsSource: Population and households: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024 1-year estimates for the metro area. Business count: Sherlock Research estimate.
reportsIntro: Each Sherlock industry report includes a city-specific data cut for Austin — local demand, competitor density, pricing benchmarks, and neighborhood-level demand patterns. One of the fastest-growing metros in the country — service demand is outpacing competitor capacity in most categories.

reportBlurbs.landscaping: Residential and commercial landscape services in Austin: demand drivers, top zip codes, pricing tiers, and competitive landscape.
reportBlurbs.roofing: Roofing market intelligence for Austin: storm cycles, insurance dynamics, reroof rates, and local competitor positioning.
reportBlurbs.hvac: HVAC service and install market for Austin: heat-pump adoption, service-plan pricing, refrigerant transition impact.
reportBlurbs.pest-control: Recurring pest control market in Austin: subscription rates, residential vs commercial mix, and local consolidation dynamics.

insights.title: Suburban build-out
insights.text: Pflugerville, Leander, Kyle, Buda, and Manor are absorbing most new residential demand. Most established operators haven't reorganized routes yet.

insights.title: Premium service tolerance
insights.text: Median household income above $90K supports premium pricing for differentiated service offerings — especially in central neighborhoods.

insights.title: Tech-employer churn
insights.text: Tech-sector layoffs softened the very top of the market. Premium demand is recovering unevenly by neighborhood, so price premium tiers street by street, not metro-wide.
